title: FERC Order Accepting Tariff Revisions in Part and Rejecting Tariff Revisions in Part, Docket ER26-3515-000
date_evidence: ORDER ACCEPTING TARIFF REVISIONS IN PART AND REJECTING TARIFF REVISIONS IN PART (Issued October 9, 2026)
key_claim: FERC accepted PJM's Large Load definition (cumulative peak of 50 MW) and registry, rejected the rest of the package including IRAS because provisions appear to place obligations on retail customers and dictate which retail customers are curtailed, ordered a compliance filing within 30 days and offered guidance should PJM refile.
frame_summary: FERC treats the choice of which retail customers are curtailed as retail regulation outside its authority, so the wholesale instrument built to start curtailment cannot stand as drafted.
verbatim_quote: certain other provisions appear to dictate which retail customers taking retail service will be curtailed
verbatim_list: establishing the threshold to qualify as a Large Load at a cumulative peak of 50 MW
require PJM to submit a compliance filing within 30 days of the date of issuance of this order
we provide guidance on how PJM could modify its proposal should PJM seek to refile it
notes: WebFetch 27/10/2026 of the order PDF hosted in PJM's eTariff directory (paragraphs 2, 14, 27, 77). Host is PJM, document is FERC's, hence the publisher label. Device network blocked, so quotes were confirmed by hand against the fetched text.

title: Tentative Order, Electric Distribution Company Interim Resource Adequacy Service, Pre-Emergency and Emergency Response Provisions (Docket M-2026-3064961)
key_claim: Pennsylvania's tentative order has distribution companies shed large computational load before other customers and keep data centres out of the exempt critical-load class, but only if FERC approves PJM's IRAS as proposed; the computational-load site test starts at 25 MW; a final order is planned for 28 January 2027.
frame_summary: Pennsylvania writes curtail-first duties as a state rule that depends on a PJM wholesale service, with the final text to follow after public comment.
verbatim_quote: If the PJM IRAS proposal is approved by FERC as proposed, jurisdictional EDCs will be required to do the following:
verbatim_list: prior to any other load shed from other customers
such that data centers are not classified as critical load exempt from curtailment
Is a customer or applicant that has an anticipated maximum peak demand of 25 MW at a single point of interconnection
A final order will be prepared for the January 28, 2027, public meeting
Comments will be due no later than 30 days after this Tentative Order is published in the Pennsylvania Bulletin
notes: WebFetch 27/10/2026. Conclusion says reply comments 15 days after comments; ordering paragraph 3 says 45 days from publication; the scan does not cite reply-comment timing. The order does not say what happens if FERC rejects IRAS.

title: PUC Advances Consumer Safeguards as Data Center Growth Adds New Demands to Electric Grid
key_claim: By a vote of 4-0 the commission approved a tentative order under which certain large new loads without new capacity would be curtailed before other customers; a final order is expected at its 28 January 2027 meeting.
frame_summary: The commission presents curtail-first as a consumer protection principle for ratepayers, not as a data-centre penalty.

title: July 22 Dominion Load Transfer Event (presentation)
key_claim: After a 230 kV line fault in the Dominion zone on 22 July 2026, approximately 3,800 MW of load transferred to back-up power, the largest load transfer PJM has experienced; PJM is evaluating potential enhancements to reliability requirements.
frame_summary: PJM frames the event as a ride-through and requirements question for the operator, not as a failure of the protection system, which it says worked.
verbatim_quote: This event was the largest load transfer PJM has experienced
verbatim_list: approximately 3,800 MW of load transferred to back-up power
PJM is evaluating potential enhancements to reliability requirements
notes: WebFetch 27/10/2026. Presentation dated July 31, 2026 (88 days before scan date); URL carries 20260730 as the committee folder.

publisher: Monitoring Analytics (Independent Market Monitor for PJM)
title: Protest of the Independent Market Monitor for PJM, Docket No. ER26-3515-000
key_claim: The market monitor asked FERC to reject IRAS, said data-centre load has added $29.4 billion to the cost of capacity, put the 2028/2029 shortfall at 6,831.3 MW, said data centres under 50 MW are 28.5 percent of data-centre peak load, and argued PJM improperly defers the curtailment decision to states.
frame_summary: The monitor argues resource adequacy across a multistate region is a federal question, so deferring the choice of curtailed customers to states is a defect rather than cooperative federalism.
verbatim_quote: The addition of data center load has resulted in adding $29.4 billion to the cost of capacity.
verbatim_list: For example, in the 2028/2029 BRA, the shortfall was 6,831.3 MW.
Data centers with peak loads less than 50 MW account for 26.8 GW or 28.5 percent of the total data center peak load.
PJM's proposal improperly defers to the states and EDCs the critical determinations of which customers will be subject to
notes: WebFetch 27/10/2026. The source's own wording 'percent' is kept in the quote; the scan writes 28.5%. Counter-position to the signal's framing: the monitor wants a federal fix.

title: PJM wants data centers to bring their own power or face cuts (Pennsylvania executive order coverage)
key_claim: Pennsylvania's governor issued an order directing the PUC to develop rules curtailing data centres before other customers; NRDC's Claire Lang-Ree said few, if any, states had taken explicit steps to align their regulatory regimes with PJM's pending proposals, while ComEd proposed an interruptible tariff.
frame_summary: The article reads Pennsylvania as the first state to turn PJM's curtail-or-bring-power idea into state process, while noting an independent commission must still write the rules.
verbatim_quote: Few, if any, have taken explicit steps to align their regulatory regimes with PJM
notes: WebFetch 27/10/2026. The 'few, if any' statement is attributed in the article to Claire Lang-Ree of NRDC and is dated 20 August 2026; the scan attributes it to her. On-page text confirmed by hand (WebFetch 27/10/2026): "Few, if any, have taken explicit steps to align their regulatory regimes with PJM's pending proposals, Lang-Ree said,". The title field is the analyst's description of the page; the article headline was not captured verbatim.

title: FERC rejects most of PJM's large load interconnection plan
key_claim: Utility Dive reports that FERC said states have a crucial role in designating which retail customers are curtailed; Commissioner Rosner said state regulators need to set clear rules for who is curtailed first; Jefferies analysts saw the proposal minimally revived, likely led by states.
frame_summary: The article reads the order as returning the curtailment-priority question to states and expects any revival to be state-led.
verbatim_quote: We need state regulators to establish clear rules for which customers should be curtailed first
verbatim_list: States have a crucial role to play in this challenge by designating which retail customers must be curtailed
We could see this proposal minimally revived in future iterations and likely led by efforts from states
notes: WebFetch 27/10/2026. The 'crucial role' sentence is the article's account of the order; the signed order excerpt reviewed does not contain it, so the scan does not cite it. On-page text confirmed by hand (WebFetch 27/10/2026): "We need state regulators to establish clear rules for which customers should be curtailed first" and "We could see this proposal minimally revived in future iterations and likely led by efforts from states".

title: FERC Accepts PJM's Large Load and Large Load Registry Definition but Rejects Interim Resource Adequacy Service Proposal
key_claim: Troutman reports Commissioner Rosner's concurrence: if PJM refiles, it must justify curtailing IRAS load on a mandatory basis before load enrolled in demand response.
frame_summary: A law-firm briefing treats the order as leaving a refiling path open and flags the unresolved priority between mandatory curtailment and voluntary demand response.
verbatim_quote: must justify curtailing IRAS load on a mandatory basis
verbatim_list: FERC directed PJM to submit within 30 days a compliance filing with only the Large Load definition and Large Load Registry
